message.content: The main bug is that the “augmented” model splines the wrong columns: its default transforms width and time, leaving the lagged-change and direction terms linear, but the current design also treats the width-by-direction interaction as an ordinary linear feature. More importantly, the matched-width contrast and bootstrap ignore time, so they can report apparent path effects caused by shared time trends; the bootstrap also resamples direction labels without recomputing them from each sampled trajectory. The revised script compares the prespecified lag model with time-and-width controls using consistent blocked folds, and estimates the matched-width contrast from a time-adjusted model on observed overlap. Its uncertainty is a moving-block bootstrap of the full original series, recomputing lag features and overlap in each replicate; all results remain descriptive for this single aggregate.
